summary: Preinstall dropper executes obfuscated payload via downloaded Bun runtime
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall = 'node setup.mjs'. setup.mjs is itself obfuscated (underscore-hex identifier style) and, at install time, downloads the Bun runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/..., chmods it executable, and execFileSyncs it against sibling file math_init.js. math_init.js is a 727KB Bun-CJS bundle heavily obfuscated with string-array shuffling (function WV8StW rotates constant table n7gIxM; identifiers such as MmgoCP, etDiOOB, JqTtnbZ). The filename math_init has no relation to the package's advertised microfrontend-loader purpose. Executing the payload via a freshly-downloaded second runtime is a common technique to evade Node-based static scanners that will not evaluate Bun-CJS output. Additionally, package.json declares files: ['dist','src'], but setup.mjs and math_init.js are shipped at the tarball root outside that allowlist — inconsistent with the maintainer's normal publish flow and consistent with a compromised-publish grafting a malicious install path onto an otherwise-legitimate library. Installing the package runs attacker-controlled, opaque code on the installer's machine.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
